main_body: Cottage: a large tiled roof slope (rows 2-43) over a plaster and timber-frame wall with a door and a window (rows 44-79)
top_band: Roof slope from row 3 to about row 41. Light ridge rows 3-8 (#e0a07c / #c97d61), then tile courses stepping darker, ending in a dark eave band at rows 38-41 and a light edge line at rows 42-43.
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large sloped surface seen from above. It has per-tile highlights, a ridge band and a chimney, and it overhangs the wall. A dark eave shadow row sits under the roof edge, and the wall below has its own tones. The stone door frame is inset, and the window has shutters and a sill. Both a top surface and a front face are clearly present. The roof has no visible side slopes, but the 3/4 contract is met.

style.evidence: The roof has about 6 tones (L 27, 65, 89, 115, 145, 175) with per-tile highlights and dark seams. The plaster has speckle, and the door has plank grain with iron bands. Outlines are tinted dark red-brown or brown, and dark edge pixels are 0% neutral. Flat-fill coverage is 2%. Median colours per tile is 10, close to the stone reference (11) and below h101 (18). Total colours (43) are lower than both references (66 and 185), so density is slightly lower, but it would sit acceptably beside the references.
